title: Learn English with Podcast | Atomic Habits for Speaking, Shadowing & Daily Fluency A2-B1

segments.text: Hello my friends.
segments.ipa: /həˈloʊ maɪ frɛndz/

segments.text: Welcome back to English Unleashed. I'm Tom.
segments.ipa: /ˈwɛlkəm bæk tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ənˈliʃt aɪm tɑm/

segments.text: In today's episode, I'm going to use the ideas from the book Atomic Habits by James Clear for language learning.
segments.ipa: /ɪn təˈdeɪz ˈɛpəˌsoʊd aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu jus ðə aɪˈdiəz frʌm ðə bʊk əˈtɑmɪk ˈhæbəts baɪ dʒeɪmz klɪr fɔr ˈlæŋɡwədʒ ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: So, I'm not only going to talk about habits in general.
segments.ipa: /soʊ aɪm nɑt ˈoʊnli ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu tɔk əˈbaʊt ˈhæbəts ɪn ˈdʒɛnərəl/

segments.text: I'm going to talk about English habits, listening habits, speaking habits.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu tɔk əˈbaʊt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈhæbəts ˈlɪsənɪŋ ˈhæbəts ˈspikɪŋ ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: Small daily habits that can slowly make your English better.
segments.ipa: /smɔl ˈdeɪli ˈhæbəts ðæt kæn ˈsloʊli meɪk jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: The main idea of Atomic Habits is simple.
segments.ipa: /ðə meɪn aɪˈdiə ʌv əˈtɑmɪk ˈhæbəts ɪz ˈsɪmpəl/

segments.text: Small habits can create big change.
segments.ipa: /smɔl ˈhæbəts kæn kriˈeɪt bɪɡ tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: The word atomic means very small.
segments.ipa: /ðə wɝd əˈtɑmɪk minz ˈvɛri smɔl/

segments.text: An atom is a very tiny thing.
segments.ipa: /æn ˈætəm ɪz ə ˈvɛri ˈtaɪni θɪŋ/

segments.text: You cannot see it with your eyes.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt si ɪt wɪð jɔr aɪz/

segments.text: But tiny things can be powerful.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈtaɪni θɪŋz kæn bi ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: Small habits are like that.
segments.ipa: /smɔl ˈhæbəts ɑr laɪk ðæt/

segments.text: They look small today.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ lʊk smɔl təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: They look too easy.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ lʊk tu ˈizi/

segments.text: They look too simple.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ lʊk tu ˈsɪmpəl/

segments.text: But when you repeat them again and again, they become powerful.
segments.ipa: /bʌt wɛn ju rɪˈpit ðɛm əˈɡɛn ənd əˈɡɛn ðeɪ bɪˈkʌm ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: This is very important for English learners.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz/

segments.text: Many learners think they need a big plan.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz θɪŋk ðeɪ nid ə bɪɡ plæn/

segments.text: They think, "I need to study English for 3 hours every day."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ θɪŋk aɪ nid tu ˈstʌdi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ fɔr ˈaʊərz ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: Or I need to move to an English-speaking country.
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪ nid tu muv tu æn English-speaking ˈkʌntri/

segments.text: Or I need to finish a big grammar book.
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪ nid tu ˈfɪnɪʃ ə bɪɡ ˈɡræmər bʊk/

segments.text: These things may help, but they're not always possible.
segments.ipa: /ðiz θɪŋz meɪ hɛlp bʌt ðɛr nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz ˈpɑsəbəl/

segments.text: Many people are busy.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl ɑr ˈbɪzi/

segments.text: They have work, family, study, stress, and daily life.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ hæv wɝk ˈfæməli ˈstʌdi strɛs ənd ˈdeɪli laɪf/

segments.text: So, when the plan is too big, they start with excitement, but they stop after a few days.
segments.ipa: /soʊ wɛn ðə plæn ɪz tu bɪɡ ðeɪ stɑrt wɪð ɪkˈsaɪtmənt bʌt ðeɪ stɑp ˈæftər ə fju deɪz/

segments.text: This is why small habits matter.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ smɔl ˈhæbəts ˈmætər/

segments.text: You do not need to change your whole life in one day.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu tʃeɪndʒ jɔr hoʊl laɪf ɪn wʌn deɪ/

segments.text: You can start with one small English habit.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn stɑrt wɪð wʌn smɔl ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈhæbət/

segments.text: Five minutes of listening.
segments.ipa: /faɪv ˈmɪnəts ʌv ˈlɪsənɪŋ/

segments.text: Three useful phrases.
segments.ipa: /θri ˈjusfəl ˈfreɪzəz/

segments.text: One short speaking answer.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ʃɔrt ˈspikɪŋ ˈænsər/

segments.text: One paragraph of reading.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ˈpærəˌɡræf ʌv ˈridɪŋ/

segments.text: One minute of shadowing.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ˈmɪnət ʌv ˈʃædoʊɪŋ/

segments.text: One small review before sleep.
segments.ipa: /wʌn smɔl ˌrivˈju bɪˈfɔr slip/

segments.text: At first, this may look too small.
segments.ipa: /æt fɝst ðɪs meɪ lʊk tu smɔl/

segments.text: You may think, "Can five minutes really help me?"
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ θɪŋk kæn faɪv ˈmɪnəts ˈrɪli hɛlp mi/

segments.text: But five minutes every day is much better than one big study session once a month.
segments.ipa: /bʌt faɪv ˈmɪnəts ˈɛvəri deɪ ɪz mʌtʃ ˈbɛtər ðæn wʌn bɪɡ ˈstʌdi ˈsɛʃən wʌns ə mʌnθ/

segments.text: Five minutes every day keeps English close to your brain.
segments.ipa: /faɪv ˈmɪnəts ˈɛvəri deɪ kips ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ kloʊs tu jɔr breɪn/

segments.text: It tells your mind, "English is part of my life."
segments.ipa: /ɪt tɛlz jɔr maɪnd ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz pɑrt ʌv maɪ laɪf/

segments.text: It builds identity.
segments.ipa: /ɪt bɪldz aɪˈdɛntɪˌti/

segments.text: It builds confidence.
segments.ipa: /ɪt bɪldz ˈkɑnfədəns/

segments.text: It builds momentum.
segments.ipa: /ɪt bɪldz moʊˈmɛntəm/

segments.text: Momentum means movement that becomes easier after it starts.
segments.ipa: /moʊˈmɛntəm minz ˈmuvmənt ðæt bɪˈkʌmz ˈiziər ˈæftər ɪt stɑrts/

segments.text: Now, a small habit is easy to repeat, and what you repeat becomes part of you.
segments.ipa: /naʊ ə smɔl ˈhæbət ɪz ˈizi tu rɪˈpit ənd wʌt ju rɪˈpit bɪˈkʌmz pɑrt ʌv ju/

segments.text: This is the heart of the book.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ðə hɑrt ʌv ðə bʊk/

segments.text: Your life is shaped by what you repeat.
segments.ipa: /jɔr laɪf ɪz ʃeɪpt baɪ wʌt ju rɪˈpit/

segments.text: Your English is also shaped by what you repeat.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz ˈɔlsoʊ ʃeɪpt baɪ wʌt ju rɪˈpit/

segments.text: If you repeat listening, your listening and speaking will improve.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju rɪˈpit ˈlɪsənɪŋ jɔr ˈlɪsənɪŋ ənd ˈspikɪŋ wɪl ˌɪmˈpruv/

segments.text: If you repeat speaking, your speaking becomes easier.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju rɪˈpit ˈspikɪŋ jɔr ˈspikɪŋ bɪˈkʌmz ˈiziər/

segments.text: If you repeat useful phrases, those phrases become natural.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju rɪˈpit ˈjusfəl ˈfreɪzəz ðoʊz ˈfreɪzəz bɪˈkʌm ˈnætʃərəl/

segments.text: If you repeat pronunciation carefully, your mouth learns the sounds.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju rɪˈpit proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən ˈkɛrfəli jɔr maʊθ lɝnz ðə saʊndz/

segments.text: But if you repeat avoiding English, avoiding becomes stronger.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju rɪˈpit əˈvɔɪdɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ əˈvɔɪdɪŋ bɪˈkʌmz ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: If you repeat saying, "I'm bad at English," that belief becomes stronger.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju rɪˈpit ˈseɪɪŋ aɪm bæd æt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ðæt bɪˈlif bɪˈkʌmz ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: If you repeat waiting for the perfect time, waiting becomes your habit.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju rɪˈpit ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr ðə pərˈfɛkt taɪm ˈweɪtɪŋ bɪˈkʌmz jɔr ˈhæbət/

segments.text: So, we need to choose better repetitions.
segments.ipa: /soʊ wi nid tu tʃuz ˈbɛtər ˌrɛpəˈtɪʃənz/

segments.text: One important idea in Atomic Habits is that we often focus too much on goals and not enough on systems.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt aɪˈdiə ɪn əˈtɑmɪk ˈhæbəts ɪz ðæt wi ˈɔfən ˈfoʊkəs tu mʌtʃ ɑn ɡoʊlz ənd nɑt ɪˈnʌf ɑn ˈsɪstəmz/

segments.text: A goal is the result you want.
segments.ipa: /ə ɡoʊl ɪz ðə rɪˈzʌlt ju wɑnt/

segments.text: For example, I want to speak English fluently.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl aɪ wɑnt tu spik ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈfluəntli/

segments.text: I want to pass IELTS test.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɑnt tu pæs IELTS tɛst/

segments.text: I want to understand movies.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɑnt tu ˌʌndərˈstænd ˈmuviz/

segments.text: I want to speak with native speakers.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɑnt tu spik wɪð ˈneɪtɪv ˈspikərz/

segments.text: These are goals.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ɑr ɡoʊlz/

segments.text: Goals are useful because they give direction.
segments.ipa: /ɡoʊlz ɑr ˈjusfəl bɪˈkɔz ðeɪ ɡɪv dərˈɛkʃən/

segments.text: But goals alone do not create progress.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɡoʊlz əˈloʊn du nɑt kriˈeɪt ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: A system is what you do every day.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈsɪstəm ɪz wʌt ju du ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: Your system is your routine.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈsɪstəm ɪz jɔr ruˈtin/

segments.text: Your system is your daily practice.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈsɪstəm ɪz jɔr ˈdeɪli ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Your system is your small repeated action.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈsɪstəm ɪz jɔr smɔl rɪˈpitɪd ˈækʃən/

segments.text: If your goal is English fluency, your system may be listening for 15 minutes every morning.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jɔr ɡoʊl ɪz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈfluənsi jɔr ˈsɪstəm meɪ bi ˈlɪsənɪŋ fɔr ˈmɪnəts ˈɛvəri ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

segments.text: Shadowing five sentences, learning three phrases, and speaking for 1 minute.
segments.ipa: /ˈʃædoʊɪŋ faɪv ˈsɛntənsəz ˈlɝnɪŋ θri ˈfreɪzəz ənd ˈspikɪŋ fɔr ˈmɪnət/

segments.text: This system creates progress.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈsɪstəm kriˈeɪts ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: A goal says, "Where do I want to go?"
segments.ipa: /ə ɡoʊl sɛz wɛr du aɪ wɑnt tu ɡoʊ/

segments.text: But a system says, what do I do today?
segments.ipa: /bʌt ə ˈsɪstəm sɛz wʌt du aɪ du təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: This is very important, my friends.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt maɪ frɛndz/

segments.text: Many learners have the same goal.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz hæv ðə seɪm ɡoʊl/

segments.text: They all want fluent English, but not all learners have the same system.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɔl wɑnt ˈfluənt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ bʌt nɑt ɔl ˈlɝnərz hæv ðə seɪm ˈsɪstəm/

segments.text: Some learners practice every day.
segments.ipa: /sʌm ˈlɝnərz ˈpræktəs ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: Some learners only dream.
segments.ipa: /sʌm ˈlɝnərz ˈoʊnli drim/

segments.text: Some learners listen, repeat, and speak.
segments.ipa: /sʌm ˈlɝnərz ˈlɪsən rɪˈpit ənd spik/

segments.text: Some learners only collect books and videos.
segments.ipa: /sʌm ˈlɝnərz ˈoʊnli kəˈlɛkt bʊks ənd ˈvɪdioʊz/

segments.text: The difference is not always the goal.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈdɪfərəns ɪz nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz ðə ɡoʊl/

segments.text: The difference is the daily system.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈdɪfərəns ɪz ðə ˈdeɪli ˈsɪstəm/

segments.text: So, in this episode, I will focus on English systems, your learning systems.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ɪn ðɪs ˈɛpəˌsoʊd aɪ wɪl ˈfoʊkəs ɑn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈsɪstəmz jɔr ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈsɪstəmz/

segments.text: We will learn how to make English habits obvious.
segments.ipa: /wi wɪl lɝn haʊ tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈhæbəts ˈɑbviəs/

segments.text: Obvious means easy to see.
segments.ipa: /ˈɑbviəs minz ˈizi tu si/

segments.text: We will learn how to make English habits attractive.
segments.ipa: /wi wɪl lɝn haʊ tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈhæbəts əˈtræktɪv/

segments.text: Attractive means something you want to do.
segments.ipa: /əˈtræktɪv minz ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju wɑnt tu du/

segments.text: We will learn how to make English habits easy and simple to start.
segments.ipa: /wi wɪl lɝn haʊ tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈhæbəts ˈizi ənd ˈsɪmpəl tu stɑrt/

segments.text: We will learn how to make English habits satisfying.
segments.ipa: /wi wɪl lɝn haʊ tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈhæbəts ˈsætɪsˌfaɪɪŋ/

segments.text: Satisfying means it gives you a good feeling after you do it.
segments.ipa: /ˈsætɪsˌfaɪɪŋ minz ɪt ɡɪvz ju ə ɡʊd ˈfilɪŋ ˈæftər ju du ɪt/

segments.text: The first big lesson in this book is this.
segments.ipa: /ðə fɝst bɪɡ ˈlɛsən ɪn ðɪs bʊk ɪz ðɪs/

segments.text: Do not wait for motivation.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt weɪt fɔr ˌmoʊtəˈveɪʃən/

segments.text: Motivation is a feeling.
segments.ipa: /ˌmoʊtəˈveɪʃən ɪz ə ˈfilɪŋ/

segments.text: Some days you feel motivated.
segments.ipa: /sʌm deɪz ju fil ˈmoʊtəˌveɪtəd/

segments.text: Some days you do not.
segments.ipa: /sʌm deɪz ju du nɑt/

segments.text: Some days you want to study.
segments.ipa: /sʌm deɪz ju wɑnt tu ˈstʌdi/

segments.text: Some days you feel tired.
segments.ipa: /sʌm deɪz ju fil ˈtaɪərd/

segments.text: If your English practice depends only on motivation, it will not be stable.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈpræktəs dɪˈpɛndz ˈoʊnli ɑn ˌmoʊtəˈveɪʃən ɪt wɪl nɑt bi ˈsteɪbəl/

segments.text: Stable means steady. It continues.
segments.ipa: /ˈsteɪbəl minz ˈstɛdi ɪt kənˈtɪnjuz/

segments.text: Habits help you continue even when motivation is low.
segments.ipa: /ˈhæbəts hɛlp ju kənˈtɪnju ˈivɪn wɛn ˌmoʊtəˈveɪʃən ɪz loʊ/

segments.text: The habit says, "That is what I do."
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈhæbət sɛz ðæt ɪz wʌt aɪ du/

segments.text: Not because I feel excited every day.
segments.ipa: /nɑt bɪˈkɔz aɪ fil ɪkˈsaɪtəd ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: Not because I am perfect, but because this action is part of my life.
segments.ipa: /nɑt bɪˈkɔz aɪ æm pərˈfɛkt bʌt bɪˈkɔz ðɪs ˈækʃən ɪz pɑrt ʌv maɪ laɪf/

segments.text: For example, brushing your teeth is a habit.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈbrʌʃɪŋ jɔr tiθ ɪz ə ˈhæbət/

segments.text: You do not need big motivation to brush your teeth.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid bɪɡ ˌmoʊtəˈveɪʃən tu brʌʃ jɔr tiθ/

segments.text: You just do it because it is part of your routine.
segments.ipa: /ju dʒʌst du ɪt bɪˈkɔz ɪt ɪz pɑrt ʌv jɔr ruˈtin/

segments.text: English can become similar.
segments.ipa: /ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ kæn bɪˈkʌm ˈsɪmələr/

segments.text: Maybe not the whole language, but one small habit can become automatic.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi nɑt ðə hoʊl ˈlæŋɡwədʒ bʌt wʌn smɔl ˈhæbət kæn bɪˈkʌm ˌɔtəˈmætɪk/

segments.text: After breakfast, I listen to English.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər ˈbrɛkfəst aɪ ˈlɪsən tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: Before sleep, I review five phrases.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈfɔr slip aɪ ˌrivˈju faɪv ˈfreɪzəz/

segments.text: After lunch, I speak for 1 minute.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər lʌntʃ aɪ spik fɔr ˈmɪnət/

segments.text: On the bus, I listen to a podcast.
segments.ipa: /ɑn ðə bʌs aɪ ˈlɪsən tu ə ˈpɔdˌkæst/

segments.text: When a habit has a place in your day, it becomes easier.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ə ˈhæbət hæz ə pleɪs ɪn jɔr deɪ ɪt bɪˈkʌmz ˈiziər/

segments.text: And this is good news.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðɪs ɪz ɡʊd nuz/

segments.text: You do not need to be a perfect learner.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu bi ə pərˈfɛkt ˈlɝnər/

segments.text: You need a small habit that you can repeat every day.
segments.ipa: /ju nid ə smɔl ˈhæbət ðæt ju kæn rɪˈpit ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: So, remember this first lesson.
segments.ipa: /soʊ rɪˈmɛmbər ðɪs fɝst ˈlɛsən/

segments.text: Better English is not built by one big study day.
segments.ipa: /ˈbɛtər ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz nɑt bɪlt baɪ wʌn bɪɡ ˈstʌdi deɪ/

segments.text: Better English is built by small habits repeated many times.
segments.ipa: /ˈbɛtər ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz bɪlt baɪ smɔl ˈhæbəts rɪˈpitɪd ˈmɛni taɪmz/

segments.text: One sentence, one phrase, one short listening practice, one small speaking answer.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ˈsɛntəns wʌn freɪz wʌn ʃɔrt ˈlɪsənɪŋ ˈpræktəs wʌn smɔl ˈspikɪŋ ˈænsər/

segments.text: Again and again.
segments.ipa: /əˈɡɛn ənd əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: That is how your English begins to change. Okay.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz haʊ jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ bɪˈɡɪnz tu tʃeɪndʒ ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: One of the deepest ideas in Atomic Habits is identity.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ʌv ðə ˈdipəst aɪˈdiəz ɪn əˈtɑmɪk ˈhæbəts ɪz aɪˈdɛntɪˌti/

segments.text: Identity means who you believe you are.
segments.ipa: /aɪˈdɛntɪˌti minz hu ju bɪˈliv ju ɑr/

segments.text: It is the story you tell yourself about yourself.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ðə ˈstɔri ju tɛl jərˈsɛlf əˈbaʊt jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: For example, someone may say, "I am a shy person."
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈsʌmˌwʌn meɪ seɪ aɪ æm ə ʃaɪ ˈpɝsən/

segments.text: Another person may say, "I am a disciplined person."
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər ˈpɝsən meɪ seɪ aɪ æm ə ˈdɪsəplənd ˈpɝsən/

segments.text: Someone may say, "I am bad at languages."
segments.ipa: /ˈsʌmˌwʌn meɪ seɪ aɪ æm bæd æt ˈlæŋɡwədʒəz/

segments.text: Another person may say, "I am becoming a better English speaker."
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər ˈpɝsən meɪ seɪ aɪ æm bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ə ˈbɛtər ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈspikər/

segments.text: These stories matter.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ˈstɔriz ˈmætər/

segments.text: They are important. Why?
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɑr ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt waɪ/

segments.text: Because your identity affects your actions.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈkɔz jɔr aɪˈdɛntɪˌti əˈfɛkts jɔr ˈækʃənz/

segments.text: If you believe, "I am bad at English," you may avoid English.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju bɪˈliv aɪ æm bæd æt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ju meɪ əˈvɔɪd ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: If you believe, "I always fail," you may stop quickly.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju bɪˈliv aɪ ˈɔlˌweɪz feɪl ju meɪ stɑp ˈkwɪkli/

segments.text: If you believe, "I cannot speak," you may stay silent even when you have a chance to practice to speak.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju bɪˈliv aɪ ˈkænɑt spik ju meɪ steɪ ˈsaɪlənt ˈivɪn wɛn ju hæv ə tʃæns tu ˈpræktəs tu spik/

segments.text: But if you believe, "I am a person who practices English every day," your actions become different.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju bɪˈliv aɪ æm ə ˈpɝsən hu ˈpræktəsəz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈɛvəri deɪ jɔr ˈækʃənz bɪˈkʌm ˈdɪfərənt/

segments.text: You do not need to be fluent.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu bi ˈfluənt/

segments.text: You do not need to be perfect.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu bi pərˈfɛkt/

segments.text: But you see yourself as someone who shows up.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ju si jərˈsɛlf æz ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu ʃoʊz ʌp/

segments.text: To show up means you come and do the work.
segments.ipa: /tu ʃoʊ ʌp minz ju kʌm ənd du ðə wɝk/

segments.text: This is very powerful.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: The author James Clear explains that habits are not only about what you want to achieve.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈɔθər dʒeɪmz klɪr ɪkˈspleɪnz ðæt ˈhæbəts ɑr nɑt ˈoʊnli əˈbaʊt wʌt ju wɑnt tu əˈtʃiv/

segments.text: They are also about who you want to become.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɑr ˈɔlsoʊ əˈbaʊt hu ju wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm/

segments.text: This is very important for language learning.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt fɔr ˈlæŋɡwədʒ ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: Do not only ask, "What level do I want?"
segments.ipa: /du nɑt ˈoʊnli æsk wʌt ˈlɛvəl du aɪ wɑnt/

segments.text: Ask, "What kind of English learner do I want to become?"
segments.ipa: /æsk wʌt kaɪnd ʌv ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnər du aɪ wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm/

segments.text: Do you want to become a learner who listens every day?
segments.ipa: /du ju wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm ə ˈlɝnər hu ˈlɪsənz ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: Do you want to become a learner who speaks even with mistakes?
segments.ipa: /du ju wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm ə ˈlɝnər hu spiks ˈivɪn wɪð mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: Do you want to become a learner who reviews vocabulary every day?
segments.ipa: /du ju wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm ə ˈlɝnər hu rivˈjuz voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: Do you want to become a learner who does not quit after one bad day?
segments.ipa: /du ju wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm ə ˈlɝnər hu dʌz nɑt kwɪt ˈæftər wʌn bæd deɪ/

segments.text: Do you want to become a learner who enjoys small progress?
segments.ipa: /du ju wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm ə ˈlɝnər hu ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪz smɔl ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: This changes the feeling of practice.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈtʃeɪndʒəz ðə ˈfilɪŋ ʌv ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: If your only focus is the goal, you may feel frustrated.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jɔr ˈoʊnli ˈfoʊkəs ɪz ðə ɡoʊl ju meɪ fil ˈfrʌˌstreɪtəd/

segments.text: You may say, "I am not advanced yet.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ seɪ aɪ æm nɑt ədˈvænst jɛt/

segments.text: I still make mistakes."
segments.ipa: /aɪ stɪl meɪk mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: But if your focus is identity, every small action becomes a vote for the person you are becoming.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf jɔr ˈfoʊkəs ɪz aɪˈdɛntɪˌti ˈɛvəri smɔl ˈækʃən bɪˈkʌmz ə voʊt fɔr ðə ˈpɝsən ju ɑr bɪˈkʌmɪŋ/

segments.text: When you listen to English for 10 minutes, you vote for the identity of an English learner.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju ˈlɪsən tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ fɔr ˈmɪnəts ju voʊt fɔr ðə aɪˈdɛntɪˌti ʌv æn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnər/

segments.text: When you repeat one sentence, you vote for the identity of a better speaker.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju rɪˈpit wʌn ˈsɛntəns ju voʊt fɔr ðə aɪˈdɛntɪˌti ʌv ə ˈbɛtər ˈspikər/

segments.text: This is a beautiful idea.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈbjutəfəl aɪˈdiə/

segments.text: You don't need to become fluent before you feel like an English learner.
segments.ipa: /ju doʊnt nid tu bɪˈkʌm ˈfluənt bɪˈfɔr ju fil laɪk æn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnər/

segments.text: You become an English learner by doing small English actions.
segments.ipa: /ju bɪˈkʌm æn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnər baɪ ˈduɪŋ smɔl ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈækʃənz/

segments.text: The identity comes from the habit.
segments.ipa: /ðə aɪˈdɛntɪˌti kʌmz frʌm ðə ˈhæbət/

segments.text: For example, if you write one sentence in English every day, you can say,
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ɪf ju raɪt wʌn ˈsɛntəns ɪn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈɛvəri deɪ ju kæn seɪ/

segments.text: "I am someone who writes in English."
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu raɪts ɪn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: Maybe the sentences are simple.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðə ˈsɛntənsəz ɑr ˈsɪmpəl/

segments.text: That is okay.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: The identity is growing.
segments.ipa: /ðə aɪˈdɛntɪˌti ɪz ˈɡroʊɪŋ/

segments.text: If you speak for 1 minute every day, you can say, "I am someone who practices speaking."
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju spik fɔr ˈmɪnət ˈɛvəri deɪ ju kæn seɪ aɪ æm ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu ˈpræktəsəz ˈspikɪŋ/

segments.text: Maybe your grammar is not perfect.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi jɔr ˈɡræmər ɪz nɑt pərˈfɛkt/

segments.text: That is okay, too.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ˌoʊˈkeɪ tu/

segments.text: The identity is growing.
segments.ipa: /ðə aɪˈdɛntɪˌti ɪz ˈɡroʊɪŋ/

segments.text: If you listen every morning, you can say English is part of my morning.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ˈlɪsən ˈɛvəri ˈmɔrnɪŋ ju kæn seɪ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz pɑrt ʌv maɪ ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

segments.text: That is beautiful.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ˈbjutəfəl/

segments.text: Many learners wait for confidence before they practice.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz weɪt fɔr ˈkɑnfədəns bɪˈfɔr ðeɪ ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: But often, confidence comes after practice.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈɔfən ˈkɑnfədəns kʌmz ˈæftər ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: You act first.
segments.ipa: /ju ækt fɝst/

segments.text: You do one small habit, then you begin to believe maybe I can do this.
segments.ipa: /ju du wʌn smɔl ˈhæbət ðɛn ju bɪˈɡɪn tu bɪˈliv ˈmeɪbi aɪ kæn du ðɪs/

segments.text: Action teaches identity.
segments.ipa: /ˈækʃən ˈtitʃəz aɪˈdɛntɪˌti/

segments.text: Let's say that again.
segments.ipa: /lɛts seɪ ðæt əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: Action teaches identity.
segments.ipa: /ˈækʃən ˈtitʃəz aɪˈdɛntɪˌti/

segments.text: So, instead of saying, "I want to be fluent."
segments.ipa: /soʊ ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈseɪɪŋ aɪ wɑnt tu bi ˈfluənt/

segments.text: say, "I am becoming someone who practices English every day."
segments.ipa: /seɪ aɪ æm bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu ˈpræktəsəz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: Instead of saying, "I want to speak perfectly."
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈseɪɪŋ aɪ wɑnt tu spik ˈpɝfəktli/

segments.text: say, "I am becoming someone who speaks even when it is not perfect."
segments.ipa: /seɪ aɪ æm bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu spiks ˈivɪn wɛn ɪt ɪz nɑt pərˈfɛkt/

segments.text: Instead of saying, "I want a better vocabulary."
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈseɪɪŋ aɪ wɑnt ə ˈbɛtər voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri/

segments.text: say, "I am becoming someone who learns words in sentences."
segments.ipa: /seɪ aɪ æm bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu lɝnz wɝdz ɪn ˈsɛntənsəz/

segments.text: And this word, becoming, is very important.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðɪs wɝd bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: It is gentle and it gives you time.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˈdʒɛntəl ənd ɪt ɡɪvz ju taɪm/

segments.text: It does not force you to be perfect today.
segments.ipa: /ɪt dʌz nɑt fɔrs ju tu bi pərˈfɛkt təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: It simply says, "You are moving in a direction."
segments.ipa: /ɪt ˈsɪmpli sɛz ju ɑr ˈmuvɪŋ ɪn ə dərˈɛkʃən/

segments.text: So, do not wait until you're ready to become a good language learner.
segments.ipa: /soʊ du nɑt weɪt ənˈtɪl jʊr ˈrɛdi tu bɪˈkʌm ə ɡʊd ˈlæŋɡwədʒ ˈlɝnər/

segments.text: Become the person by doing the action.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈkʌm ðə ˈpɝsən baɪ ˈduɪŋ ðə ˈækʃən/

segments.text: Another important idea is that your old identity may try to pull you back.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt aɪˈdiə ɪz ðæt jɔr oʊld aɪˈdɛntɪˌti meɪ traɪ tu pʊl ju bæk/

segments.text: What does that mean?
segments.ipa: /wʌt dʌz ðæt min/

segments.text: Maybe you have said for many years, "I'm not good at English."
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju hæv sɛd fɔr ˈmɛni jɪrz aɪm nɑt ɡʊd æt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: Maybe a teacher corrected you harshly.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ə ˈtitʃər kərˈɛktəd ju ˈhɑrʃli/

segments.text: Maybe someone laughed at your pronunciation.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ˈsʌmˌwʌn læft æt jɔr proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən/

segments.text: Maybe you failed an exam.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju feɪld æn ɪɡˈzæm/

segments.text: Maybe you studied for years, but did not speak.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju ˈstʌdid fɔr jɪrz bʌt dɪd nɑt spik/

segments.text: Now this old identity feels familiar.
segments.ipa: /naʊ ðɪs oʊld aɪˈdɛntɪˌti filz fəˈmɪljər/

segments.text: It feels normal.
segments.ipa: /ɪt filz ˈnɔrməl/

segments.text: But familiar does not mean true forever.
segments.ipa: /bʌt fəˈmɪljər dʌz nɑt min tru fərˈɛvər/

segments.text: You can build a new identity with new evidence.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn bɪld ə nu aɪˈdɛntɪˌti wɪð nu ˈɛvədəns/

segments.text: Small habits create new evidence.
segments.ipa: /smɔl ˈhæbəts kriˈeɪt nu ˈɛvədəns/

segments.text: This is why very small habits are important.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ ˈvɛri smɔl ˈhæbəts ɑr ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: They truly matter.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ˈtruli ˈmætər/

segments.text: They may look tiny, but they are changing your story.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ meɪ lʊk ˈtaɪni bʌt ðeɪ ɑr ˈtʃeɪndʒɪŋ jɔr ˈstɔri/

segments.text: Imagine you say, "I am someone who never studies."
segments.ipa: /ˌɪˈmædʒən ju seɪ aɪ æm ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu ˈnɛvər ˈstʌdiz/

segments.text: Then you study for 5 minutes every day for 2 weeks.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ju ˈstʌdi fɔr ˈmɪnəts ˈɛvəri deɪ fɔr wiks/

segments.text: Now your brain has new evidence.
segments.ipa: /naʊ jɔr breɪn hæz nu ˈɛvədəns/

segments.text: It has a new story.
segments.ipa: /ɪt hæz ə nu ˈstɔri/

segments.text: The old story becomes weaker.
segments.ipa: /ðə oʊld ˈstɔri bɪˈkʌmz ˈwikər/

segments.text: The new story becomes stronger.
segments.ipa: /ðə nu ˈstɔri bɪˈkʌmz ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: "I can practice.
segments.ipa: /aɪ kæn ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: I can return.
segments.ipa: /aɪ kæn rɪˈtɝn/

segments.text: I can learn.
segments.ipa: /aɪ kæn lɝn/

segments.text: I can improve.
segments.ipa: /aɪ kæn ˌɪmˈpruv/

segments.text: I am becoming a confident English speaker.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ə ˈkɑnfədənt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈspikər/

segments.text: I am becoming a consistent English learner.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ə kənˈsɪstənt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnər/

segments.text: This is who I am becoming." All right.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz hu aɪ æm bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ɔl raɪt/

segments.text: Now let's talk about the first law of habits.
segments.ipa: /naʊ lɛts tɔk əˈbaʊt ðə fɝst lɔ ʌv ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: The first law is this.
segments.ipa: /ðə fɝst lɔ ɪz ðɪs/

segments.text: Make it obvious.
segments.ipa: /meɪk ɪt ˈɑbviəs/

segments.text: Obvious means easy to see, easy to notice, easy to remember.
segments.ipa: /ˈɑbviəs minz ˈizi tu si ˈizi tu ˈnoʊtəs ˈizi tu rɪˈmɛmbər/

segments.text: Many people do not practice English because English is not visible in their daily life.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl du nɑt ˈpræktəs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ bɪˈkɔz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz nɑt ˈvɪzəbəl ɪn ðɛr ˈdeɪli laɪf/

segments.text: Their books are closed.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr bʊks ɑr kloʊzd/

segments.text: Their podcast is not ready.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr ˈpɔdˌkæst ɪz nɑt ˈrɛdi/

segments.text: Their phone is full of other things.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr foʊn ɪz fʊl ʌv ˈʌðər θɪŋz/

segments.text: Their day begins and ends without any clear reminder to practice.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr deɪ bɪˈɡɪnz ənd ɛndz wɪˈθaʊt ˈɛni klɪr riˈmaɪndər tu ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Then they say, "I forgot."
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ðeɪ seɪ aɪ fərˈɡɑt/

segments.text: or "I was busy."
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪ wɑz ˈbɪzi/

segments.text: or "I did not have time."
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪ dɪd nɑt hæv taɪm/

segments.text: But often, the problem is not time only.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈɔfən ðə ˈprɑbləm ɪz nɑt taɪm ˈoʊnli/

segments.text: The problem is that the habit has no clear place in the day.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑbləm ɪz ðæt ðə ˈhæbət hæz noʊ klɪr pleɪs ɪn ðə deɪ/

segments.text: A habit needs a cue.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈhæbət nidz ə kju/

segments.text: What is a cue?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪz ə kju/

segments.text: A cue is a signal.
segments.ipa: /ə kju ɪz ə ˈsɪɡnəl/

segments.text: It tells your brain, "Now it is time to do this."
segments.ipa: /ɪt tɛlz jɔr breɪn naʊ ɪt ɪz taɪm tu du ðɪs/

segments.text: For example, feeling tired may be a cue to drink coffee.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈfilɪŋ ˈtaɪərd meɪ bi ə kju tu drɪŋk ˈkɑfi/

segments.text: Sitting on a sofa may be a cue to open social media.
segments.ipa: /ˈsɪtɪŋ ɑn ə ˈsoʊfə meɪ bi ə kju tu ˈoʊpən ˈsoʊʃəl ˈmidiə/

segments.text: Going to bed may be a cue to check your phone.
segments.ipa: /ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu bɛd meɪ bi ə kju tu tʃɛk jɔr foʊn/

segments.text: Cues already control many habits.
segments.ipa: /kjuz ɔlˈrɛdi kənˈtroʊl ˈmɛni ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: So, we can use cues to build English habits.
segments.ipa: /soʊ wi kæn jus kjuz tu bɪld ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: A very useful method is called habit stacking.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈvɛri ˈjusfəl ˈmɛθəd ɪz kɔld ˈhæbət ˈstækɪŋ/

segments.text: Habit stacking means you connect a new habit to an old habit.
segments.ipa: /ˈhæbət ˈstækɪŋ minz ju kəˈnɛkt ə nu ˈhæbət tu æn oʊld ˈhæbət/

segments.text: You take something you already do every day and you put English right after it.
segments.ipa: /ju teɪk ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju ɔlˈrɛdi du ˈɛvəri deɪ ənd ju pʊt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ raɪt ˈæftər ɪt/

segments.text: For example, after I make coffee, I will listen to English for 5 minutes.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈæftər aɪ meɪk ˈkɑfi aɪ wɪl ˈlɪsən tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: After I brush my teeth, I will repeat five English sentences.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər aɪ brʌʃ maɪ tiθ aɪ wɪl rɪˈpit faɪv ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈsɛntənsəz/

segments.text: After lunch, I will write three English sentences.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər lʌntʃ aɪ wɪl raɪt θri ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈsɛntənsəz/

segments.text: After I sit on the bus, I will listen to an English podcast.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər aɪ sɪt ɑn ðə bʌs aɪ wɪl ˈlɪsən tu æn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈpɔdˌkæst/

segments.text: After I open my laptop, I will review one vocabulary note.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər aɪ ˈoʊpən maɪ ˈlæpˌtɑp aɪ wɪl ˌrivˈju wʌn voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri noʊt/

segments.text: You do not need to ask, "When should I practice?"
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu æsk wɛn ʃʊd aɪ ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: You already know.
segments.ipa: /ju ɔlˈrɛdi noʊ/

segments.text: After coffee, after breakfast, after lunch, before sleep, on the bus, during a walk.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər ˈkɑfi ˈæftər ˈbrɛkfəst ˈæftər lʌntʃ bɪˈfɔr slip ɑn ðə bʌs ˈdʊrɪŋ ə wɔk/

segments.text: A clear time and place make habits easier.
segments.ipa: /ə klɪr taɪm ənd pleɪs meɪk ˈhæbəts ˈiziər/

segments.text: Do not say only, "I will study English more."
segments.ipa: /du nɑt seɪ ˈoʊnli aɪ wɪl ˈstʌdi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ mɔr/

segments.text: This is too general.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz tu ˈdʒɛnərəl/

segments.text: Say, "After breakfast, I will listen to English for 5 minutes."
segments.ipa: /seɪ ˈæftər ˈbrɛkfəst aɪ wɪl ˈlɪsən tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: This is specific.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz spəˈsɪfɪk/

segments.text: Specific means clear.
segments.ipa: /spəˈsɪfɪk minz klɪr/

segments.text: A clear plan helps the brain.
segments.ipa: /ə klɪr plæn hɛlps ðə breɪn/

segments.text: Another way to make English obvious is to design your environment.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər weɪ tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈɑbviəs ɪz tu dɪˈzaɪn jɔr ɪnˈvaɪrənmənt/

segments.text: Environment means the space around you.
segments.ipa: /ɪnˈvaɪrənmənt minz ðə speɪs ərˈaʊnd ju/

segments.text: Your room, your desk, your phone, your bag, your car, your kitchen, your daily tools, right?
segments.ipa: /jɔr rum jɔr dɛsk jɔr foʊn jɔr bæɡ jɔr kɑr jɔr ˈkɪtʃən jɔr ˈdeɪli tulz raɪt/

segments.text: If your environment makes English easy to see, you will practice more.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jɔr ɪnˈvaɪrənmənt meɪks ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈizi tu si ju wɪl ˈpræktəs mɔr/

segments.text: So, put your English notebook on your desk.
segments.ipa: /soʊ pʊt jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈnoʊtˌbʊk ɑn jɔr dɛsk/

segments.text: Keep your headphones beside your bed.
segments.ipa: /kip jɔr ˈhɛdˌfoʊnz bɪˈsaɪd jɔr bɛd/

segments.text: Save your favorite English podcast on your phone.
segments.ipa: /seɪv jɔr ˈfeɪvərɪt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈpɔdˌkæst ɑn jɔr foʊn/

segments.text: Keep one English book near your chair.
segments.ipa: /kip wʌn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ bʊk nɪr jɔr tʃɛr/

segments.text: Many people think they need more motivation, but sometimes they need a better environment.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl θɪŋk ðeɪ nid mɔr ˌmoʊtəˈveɪʃən bʌt səmˈtaɪmz ðeɪ nid ə ˈbɛtər ɪnˈvaɪrənmənt/

segments.text: If the good habit is invisible, you cannot see it and you forget it.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ðə ɡʊd ˈhæbət ɪz ˌɪnˈvɪzəbəl ju ˈkænɑt si ɪt ənd ju fərˈɡɛt ɪt/

segments.text: If the good habit is visible, you remember it.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ðə ɡʊd ˈhæbət ɪz ˈvɪzəbəl ju rɪˈmɛmbər ɪt/

segments.text: For example, if your guitar is in the closet, you may not play.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ɪf jɔr ɡɪˈtɑr ɪz ɪn ðə ˈklɑzət ju meɪ nɑt pleɪ/

segments.text: If it is in the room, ready, you may play more.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ɪt ɪz ɪn ðə rum ˈrɛdi ju meɪ pleɪ mɔr/

segments.text: If your English notebook is hidden, you may not write.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈnoʊtˌbʊk ɪz ˈhɪdən ju meɪ nɑt raɪt/

segments.text: If it is open on your desk, writing becomes easier.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ɪt ɪz ˈoʊpən ɑn jɔr dɛsk ˈraɪtɪŋ bɪˈkʌmz ˈiziər/

segments.text: So, make the good habit visible.
segments.ipa: /soʊ meɪk ðə ɡʊd ˈhæbət ˈvɪzəbəl/

segments.text: This is simple, but very effective.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈsɪmpəl bʌt ˈvɛri ɪˈfɛktɪv/

segments.text: You can also make bad habits less obvious.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈɔlsoʊ meɪk bæd ˈhæbəts lɛs ˈɑbviəs/

segments.text: If your phone distracts you from English, put it in another room for 10 minutes.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jɔr foʊn dɪˈstrækts ju frʌm ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ pʊt ɪt ɪn əˈnʌðər rum fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: If social media takes your listening time, move the app away from the home screen.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈsoʊʃəl ˈmidiə teɪks jɔr ˈlɪsənɪŋ taɪm muv ðə æp əˈweɪ frʌm ðə hoʊm skrin/

segments.text: Create a special playlist with only English learning videos.
segments.ipa: /kriˈeɪt ə ˈspɛʃəl ˈpleɪlɪst wɪð ˈoʊnli ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈvɪdioʊz/

segments.text: You do not need to fight temptation every minute.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu faɪt tɛmˈteɪʃən ˈɛvəri ˈmɪnət/

segments.text: Design your environment so the better choice is easier.
segments.ipa: /dɪˈzaɪn jɔr ɪnˈvaɪrənmənt soʊ ðə ˈbɛtər tʃɔɪs ɪz ˈiziər/

segments.text: Temptation means something that pulls you towards a habit, often a habit that is not helpful. Okay.
segments.ipa: /tɛmˈteɪʃən minz ˈsʌmθɪŋ ðæt pʊlz ju təˈwɔrdz ə ˈhæbət ˈɔfən ə ˈhæbət ðæt ɪz nɑt ˈhɛlpfəl ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: Now, let's talk about the second law of habits.
segments.ipa: /naʊ lɛts tɔk əˈbaʊt ðə ˈsɛkənd lɔ ʌv ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: Make it attractive.
segments.ipa: /meɪk ɪt əˈtræktɪv/

segments.text: The first law was to make it obvious.
segments.ipa: /ðə fɝst lɔ wɑz tu meɪk ɪt ˈɑbviəs/

segments.text: The second law is to make it attractive.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈsɛkənd lɔ ɪz tu meɪk ɪt əˈtræktɪv/

segments.text: Attractive means you want to do it.
segments.ipa: /əˈtræktɪv minz ju wɑnt tu du ɪt/

segments.text: It feels pleasant, interesting, enjoyable, or meaningful.
segments.ipa: /ɪt filz ˈplɛzənt ˈɪntrəstɪŋ ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪəbəl ɔr ˈminɪŋfəl/

segments.text: If a habit feels horrible every time, it is harder to repeat.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ə ˈhæbət filz ˈhɔrəbəl ˈɛvəri taɪm ɪt ɪz ˈhɑrdər tu rɪˈpit/

segments.text: If a habit feels good, it becomes easier.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ə ˈhæbət filz ɡʊd ɪt bɪˈkʌmz ˈiziər/

segments.text: Many English learners make English too painful.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ tu ˈpeɪnfəl/

segments.text: They choose very difficult materials.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ tʃuz ˈvɛri ˈdɪfəkəlt məˈtɪriəlz/

segments.text: They force themselves to memorize long sentences or long lists of vocabulary.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ fɔrs ðɛmˈsɛlvz tu ˈmɛmərˌaɪz lɔŋ ˈsɛntənsəz ɔr lɔŋ lɪsts ʌv voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri/

segments.text: They study grammar in a dry way.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ˈstʌdi ˈɡræmər ɪn ə draɪ weɪ/

segments.text: They compare themselves with advanced speakers.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ kəmˈpɛr ðɛmˈsɛlvz wɪð ədˈvænst ˈspikərz/

segments.text: They feel bad after every mistake.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ fil bæd ˈæftər ˈɛvəri mɪˈsteɪk/

segments.text: Then English becomes connected with stress.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ bɪˈkʌmz kəˈnɛktɪd wɪð strɛs/

segments.text: When English feels like stress, the brain wants to avoid it.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ filz laɪk strɛs ðə breɪn wɑnts tu əˈvɔɪd ɪt/

segments.text: So, we need to make English more attractive.
segments.ipa: /soʊ wi nid tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ mɔr əˈtræktɪv/

segments.text: This does not mean English practice must always be entertainment.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs dʌz nɑt min ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈpræktəs mʌst ˈɔlˌweɪz bi ˌɛntərˈteɪnmənt/

segments.text: No, it does not mean you only do easy things.
segments.ipa: /noʊ ɪt dʌz nɑt min ju ˈoʊnli du ˈizi θɪŋz/

segments.text: Growth needs effort, but effort can still feel meaningful and enjoyable.
segments.ipa: /ɡroʊθ nidz ˈɛfərt bʌt ˈɛfərt kæn stɪl fil ˈminɪŋfəl ənd ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪəbəl/

segments.text: Practice can be useful and pleasant at the same time.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs kæn bi ˈjusfəl ənd ˈplɛzənt æt ðə seɪm taɪm/

segments.text: One way to make English attractive is to connect it with something you already enjoy.
segments.ipa: /wʌn weɪ tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ əˈtræktɪv ɪz tu kəˈnɛkt ɪt wɪð ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju ɔlˈrɛdi ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ/

segments.text: If you like stories, learn English through stories.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju laɪk ˈstɔriz lɝn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ θru ˈstɔriz/

segments.text: If you like personal growth, listen to easy English book summaries.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju laɪk ˈpɝsɪnəl ɡroʊθ ˈlɪsən tu ˈizi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ bʊk ˈsʌməriz/

segments.text: If you like movies, learn English through movie scenes.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju laɪk ˈmuviz lɝn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ θru ˈmuvi sinz/

segments.text: If you like music, use songs carefully.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju laɪk ˈmjuzɪk jus sɔŋz ˈkɛrfəli/

segments.text: If you like psychology, listen to simple psychology podcasts.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju laɪk saɪˈkɑlədʒi ˈlɪsən tu ˈsɪmpəl saɪˈkɑlədʒi podcasts/

segments.text: If you like daily life topics, listen to conversations about routines, food, work, friendship, and travel.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju laɪk ˈdeɪli laɪf ˈtɑpɪks ˈlɪsən tu ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃənz əˈbaʊt ruˈtinz fud wɝk ˈfrɛndʃɪp ənd ˈtrævəl/

segments.text: The topic matters.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈtɑpɪk ˈmætərz/

segments.text: When the topic is interesting, you want to continue.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ðə ˈtɑpɪk ɪz ˈɪntrəstɪŋ ju wɑnt tu kənˈtɪnju/

segments.text: Your attention becomes stronger.
segments.ipa: /jɔr əˈtɛnʃən bɪˈkʌmz ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: Your brain remembers more because the meaning matters to you.
segments.ipa: /jɔr breɪn rɪˈmɛmbərz mɔr bɪˈkɔz ðə ˈminɪŋ ˈmætərz tu ju/

segments.text: For example, learning the word habit from a boring list may not be exciting.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈlɝnɪŋ ðə wɝd ˈhæbət frʌm ə ˈbɔrɪŋ lɪst meɪ nɑt bi ɪkˈsaɪtɪŋ/

segments.text: But hearing it in a sentence like a small habit can change your English feels more meaningful.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈhirɪŋ ɪt ɪn ə ˈsɛntəns laɪk ə smɔl ˈhæbət kæn tʃeɪndʒ jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ filz mɔr ˈminɪŋfəl/

segments.text: You understand the word inside an idea.
segments.ipa: /ju ˌʌndərˈstænd ðə wɝd ˌɪnˈsaɪd æn aɪˈdiə/

segments.text: You remember it better.
segments.ipa: /ju rɪˈmɛmbər ɪt ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: This is why learning vocabulary in context is so powerful.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ ˈlɝnɪŋ voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri ɪn ˈkɑntɛkst ɪz soʊ ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: Context means the situation around the word.
segments.ipa: /ˈkɑntɛkst minz ðə ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən ərˈaʊnd ðə wɝd/

segments.text: It helps you understand and remember.
segments.ipa: /ɪt hɛlps ju ˌʌndərˈstænd ənd rɪˈmɛmbər/

segments.text: Another way to make English attractive is to connect English to something you like to do.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər weɪ tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ əˈtræktɪv ɪz tu kəˈnɛkt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ tu ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju laɪk tu du/

segments.text: For example, I listen to English while drinking coffee.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl aɪ ˈlɪsən tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ waɪl ˈdrɪŋkɪŋ ˈkɑfi/

segments.text: I practice shadowing while walking in the park.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈpræktəs ˈʃædoʊɪŋ waɪl ˈwɔkɪŋ ɪn ðə pɑrk/

segments.text: I review vocabulary after I make tea.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˌrivˈju voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri ˈæftər aɪ meɪk ti/

segments.text: I watch one English lesson before watching entertainment.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɑtʃ wʌn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɛsən bɪˈfɔr ˈwɑtʃɪŋ ˌɛntərˈteɪnmənt/

segments.text: You are connecting English with a pleasant moment.
segments.ipa: /ju ɑr kəˈnɛktɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ wɪð ə ˈplɛzənt ˈmoʊmənt/

segments.text: This makes the habit easier to repeat.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs meɪks ðə ˈhæbət ˈiziər tu rɪˈpit/

segments.text: For many learners, listening is the easiest habit to make attractive.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz ˈlɪsənɪŋ ɪz ðə ˈiziəst ˈhæbət tu meɪk əˈtræktɪv/

segments.text: You can listen while walking, driving, cooking, cleaning, or resting.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈlɪsən waɪl ˈwɔkɪŋ ˈdraɪvɪŋ ˈkʊkɪŋ ˈklinɪŋ ɔr ˈrɛstɪŋ/

segments.text: You can choose a calm voice.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn tʃuz ə kɑm vɔɪs/

segments.text: You can choose interesting topics.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn tʃuz ˈɪntrəstɪŋ ˈtɑpɪks/

segments.text: You can make English part of a peaceful routine.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ pɑrt ʌv ə ˈpisfəl ruˈtin/

segments.text: But remember, passive listening and active listening are different.
segments.ipa: /bʌt rɪˈmɛmbər ˈpæsɪv ˈlɪsənɪŋ ənd ˈæktɪv ˈlɪsənɪŋ ɑr ˈdɪfərənt/

segments.text: Passive listening means English is in the background.
segments.ipa: /ˈpæsɪv ˈlɪsənɪŋ minz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz ɪn ðə ˈbækˌɡraʊnd/

segments.text: Active listening means you pay attention.
segments.ipa: /ˈæktɪv ˈlɪsənɪŋ minz ju peɪ əˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: Both will help, but for growth, you need some active listening, too.
segments.ipa: /boʊθ wɪl hɛlp bʌt fɔr ɡroʊθ ju nid sʌm ˈæktɪv ˈlɪsənɪŋ tu/

segments.text: So, you can make a habit like this.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ju kæn meɪk ə ˈhæbət laɪk ðɪs/

segments.text: First, listen casually while walking.
segments.ipa: /fɝst ˈlɪsən ˈkæʒəwəli waɪl ˈwɔkɪŋ/

segments.text: Then, choose one small part and repeat it carefully.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn tʃuz wʌn smɔl pɑrt ənd rɪˈpit ɪt ˈkɛrfəli/

segments.text: It's attractive and useful.
segments.ipa: /ɪts əˈtræktɪv ənd ˈjusfəl/

segments.text: Another important idea is to make progress feel good.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt aɪˈdiə ɪz tu meɪk ˈprɑˌɡrɛs fil ɡʊd/

segments.text: Many learners only notice what they cannot do.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz ˈoʊnli ˈnoʊtəs wʌt ðeɪ ˈkænɑt du/

segments.text: They say, "I still cannot understand everything.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ aɪ stɪl ˈkænɑt ˌʌndərˈstænd ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ/

segments.text: I still make mistakes.
segments.ipa: /aɪ stɪl meɪk mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: I still cannot speak fast."
segments.ipa: /aɪ stɪl ˈkænɑt spik fæst/

segments.text: This makes practice feel heavy.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs meɪks ˈpræktəs fil ˈhɛvi/

segments.text: Instead, notice small wins.
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd ˈnoʊtəs smɔl wɪnz/

segments.text: A small win means a small success.
segments.ipa: /ə smɔl wɪn minz ə smɔl səkˈsɛs/

segments.text: You understood one new phrase.
segments.ipa: /ju ˌʌndərˈstʊd wʌn nu freɪz/

segments.text: That is a win.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ə wɪn/

segments.text: You listened for 10 minutes.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈlɪsənd fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: That is a win.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ə wɪn/

segments.text: You spoke for 1 minute.
segments.ipa: /ju spoʊk fɔr ˈmɪnət/

segments.text: That is also a win.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ˈɔlsoʊ ə wɪn/

segments.text: When you notice small wins, English becomes more attractive.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju ˈnoʊtəs smɔl wɪnz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ bɪˈkʌmz mɔr əˈtræktɪv/

segments.text: Your brain begins to connect practice with success, not difficulty.
segments.ipa: /jɔr breɪn bɪˈɡɪnz tu kəˈnɛkt ˈpræktəs wɪð səkˈsɛs nɑt ˈdɪfəkəlti/

segments.text: This does not mean you lie to yourself.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs dʌz nɑt min ju laɪ tu jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: You still know you need improvement.
segments.ipa: /ju stɪl noʊ ju nid ˌɪmˈpruvmənt/

segments.text: But you also respect progress.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ju ˈɔlsoʊ rɪˈspɛkt ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: Both are important.
segments.ipa: /boʊθ ɑr ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: Another way to make English attractive is to join a group or community.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər weɪ tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ əˈtræktɪv ɪz tu dʒɔɪn ə ɡrup ɔr kəmˈjunəti/

segments.text: People around us affect our habits.
segments.ipa: /ˈpipəl ərˈaʊnd ʌs əˈfɛkt ˈaʊər ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: If you are around people who practice English, English feels more normal.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ɑr ərˈaʊnd ˈpipəl hu ˈpræktəs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ filz mɔr ˈnɔrməl/

segments.text: If you follow channels, teachers, or learners who make English enjoyable, you feel more motivated.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ˈfɑloʊ ˈtʃænəlz ˈtitʃərz ɔr ˈlɝnərz hu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪəbəl ju fil mɔr ˈmoʊtəˌveɪtəd/

segments.text: A community can be online or offline.
segments.ipa: /ə kəmˈjunəti kæn bi ˈɔnˌlaɪn ɔr ˈɔˌflaɪn/

segments.text: It can be a class or a speaking group.
segments.ipa: /ɪt kæn bi ə klæs ɔr ə ˈspikɪŋ ɡrup/

segments.text: It can even be a YouTube channel, a podcast audience, a friend, or even one study partner.
segments.ipa: /ɪt kæn ˈivɪn bi ə ˈjutˌjub ˈtʃænəl ə ˈpɔdˌkæst ˈɑdiəns ə frɛnd ɔr ˈivɪn wʌn ˈstʌdi ˈpɑrtnər/

segments.text: The point is this.
segments.ipa: /ðə pɔɪnt ɪz ðɪs/

segments.text: When English is connected to people and identity, it becomes stronger.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz kəˈnɛktɪd tu ˈpipəl ənd aɪˈdɛntɪˌti ɪt bɪˈkʌmz ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: You begin to think, "People like me practice English."
segments.ipa: /ju bɪˈɡɪn tu θɪŋk ˈpipəl laɪk mi ˈpræktəs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: And that is powerful.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðæt ɪz ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: If your friends never study, it is harder to study.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jɔr frɛndz ˈnɛvər ˈstʌdi ɪt ɪz ˈhɑrdər tu ˈstʌdi/

segments.text: If your environment supports learning, it becomes easier.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jɔr ɪnˈvaɪrənmənt səˈpɔrts ˈlɝnɪŋ ɪt bɪˈkʌmz ˈiziər/

segments.text: So, choose your influences carefully.
segments.ipa: /soʊ tʃuz jɔr ˈɪnˌfluənsɪz ˈkɛrfəli/

segments.text: Follow content that encourages you.
segments.ipa: /ˈfɑloʊ ˈkɑntɛnt ðæt ɛnˈkɝɪdʒɪz ju/

segments.text: Listen to teachers who make English clear.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən tu ˈtitʃərz hu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ klɪr/

segments.text: Spend time with learners who are serious but kind.
segments.ipa: /spɛnd taɪm wɪð ˈlɝnərz hu ɑr ˈsɪriəs bʌt kaɪnd/

segments.text: Attractive habits are often social habits.
segments.ipa: /əˈtræktɪv ˈhæbəts ɑr ˈɔfən ˈsoʊʃəl ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: Another important point is to reduce negative feelings around mistakes.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt pɔɪnt ɪz tu rəˈdus ˈnɛɡətɪv ˈfilɪŋz ərˈaʊnd mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: If every mistake feels like shame, speaking becomes unattractive.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈɛvəri mɪˈsteɪk filz laɪk ʃeɪm ˈspikɪŋ bɪˈkʌmz ˌʌnəˈtræktɪv/

segments.text: You avoid it.
segments.ipa: /ju əˈvɔɪd ɪt/

segments.text: You stay quiet. You wait.
segments.ipa: /ju steɪ ˈkwaɪət ju weɪt/

segments.text: But if mistakes feel like learning, speaking becomes easier.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf mɪˈsteɪks fil laɪk ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈspikɪŋ bɪˈkʌmz ˈiziər/

segments.text: Change the meaning of mistakes.
segments.ipa: /tʃeɪndʒ ðə ˈminɪŋ ʌv mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: A mistake is not a proof that you are bad at English.
segments.ipa: /ə mɪˈsteɪk ɪz nɑt ə pruf ðæt ju ɑr bæd æt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: A mistake is proof that you are learning.
segments.ipa: /ə mɪˈsteɪk ɪz pruf ðæt ju ɑr ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: A mistake is proof that you are using the language.
segments.ipa: /ə mɪˈsteɪk ɪz pruf ðæt ju ɑr ˈjuzɪŋ ðə ˈlæŋɡwədʒ/

segments.text: A mistake shows that you are practicing.
segments.ipa: /ə mɪˈsteɪk ʃoʊz ðæt ju ɑr ˈpræktəsɪŋ/

segments.text: This new meaning makes practice less scary.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs nu ˈminɪŋ meɪks ˈpræktəs lɛs ˈskɛri/

segments.text: When practice is less scary, it becomes more attractive.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ˈpræktəs ɪz lɛs ˈskɛri ɪt bɪˈkʌmz mɔr əˈtræktɪv/

segments.text: Okay, now we come to the third law of habits.
segments.ipa: /ˌoʊˈkeɪ naʊ wi kʌm tu ðə θɝd lɔ ʌv ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: Make it easy.
segments.ipa: /meɪk ɪt ˈizi/

segments.text: This may be the most important law for busy English learners.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs meɪ bi ðə moʊst ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt lɔ fɔr ˈbɪzi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz/

segments.text: Many people fail because they make the habit too hard.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl feɪl bɪˈkɔz ðeɪ meɪk ðə ˈhæbət tu hɑrd/

segments.text: They want to study for 2 hours.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ wɑnt tu ˈstʌdi fɔr ˈaʊərz/

segments.text: They want to memorize too many words.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ wɑnt tu ˈmɛmərˌaɪz tu ˈmɛni wɝdz/

segments.text: They want to watch difficult movies.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ wɑnt tu wɑtʃ ˈdɪfəkəlt ˈmuviz/

segments.text: They want to speak perfectly from the beginning.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ wɑnt tu spik ˈpɝfəktli frʌm ðə bɪˈɡɪnɪŋ/

segments.text: The habit becomes heavy.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈhæbət bɪˈkʌmz ˈhɛvi/

segments.text: Then they stop.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ðeɪ stɑp/

segments.text: A habit should be easy to start.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈhæbət ʃʊd bi ˈizi tu stɑrt/

segments.text: This is very important.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: Starting is often the hardest part.
segments.ipa: /ˈstɑrtɪŋ ɪz ˈɔfən ðə ˈhɑrdəst pɑrt/

segments.text: When you begin, you may continue.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju bɪˈɡɪn ju meɪ kənˈtɪnju/

segments.text: But if the beginning feels too difficult, you may not begin at all.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ðə bɪˈɡɪnɪŋ filz tu ˈdɪfəkəlt ju meɪ nɑt bɪˈɡɪn æt ɔl/

segments.text: James Clear talks about making the habit very small.
segments.ipa: /dʒeɪmz klɪr tɔks əˈbaʊt ˈmeɪkɪŋ ðə ˈhæbət ˈvɛri smɔl/

segments.text: For language learning, this is perfect.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈlæŋɡwədʒ ˈlɝnɪŋ ðɪs ɪz pərˈfɛkt/

segments.text: You can create a 2-minute English habit.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn kriˈeɪt ə ˈmɪnət ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈhæbət/

segments.text: 2 minutes sounds too easy.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɪnəts saʊndz tu ˈizi/

segments.text: But that is the point.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðæt ɪz ðə pɔɪnt/

segments.text: It is easy enough to do even when you are tired.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˈizi ɪˈnʌf tu du ˈivɪn wɛn ju ɑr ˈtaɪərd/

segments.text: For example, open your English notebook, listen to 1 minute of English, repeat one sentence,
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈoʊpən jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈnoʊtˌbʊk ˈlɪsən tu ˈmɪnət ʌv ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ rɪˈpit wʌn ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: write one English sentence, review one phrase, read one short paragraph.
segments.ipa: /raɪt wʌn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈsɛntəns ˌrivˈju wʌn freɪz rɛd wʌn ʃɔrt ˈpærəˌɡræf/

segments.text: These are small actions, but they start the habit.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ɑr smɔl ˈækʃənz bʌt ðeɪ stɑrt ðə ˈhæbət/

segments.text: And once you start, you often do more.
segments.ipa: /ənd wʌns ju stɑrt ju ˈɔfən du mɔr/

segments.text: The goal is not to study only 2 minutes forever.
segments.ipa: /ðə ɡoʊl ɪz nɑt tu ˈstʌdi ˈoʊnli ˈmɪnəts fərˈɛvər/

segments.text: The goal is to make starting easy.
segments.ipa: /ðə ɡoʊl ɪz tu meɪk ˈstɑrtɪŋ ˈizi/

segments.text: A small start can become a longer session naturally.
segments.ipa: /ə smɔl stɑrt kæn bɪˈkʌm ə ˈlɔŋɡər ˈsɛʃən ˈnætʃərəli/

segments.text: But even if it stays small, you have kept the habit alive.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈivɪn ɪf ɪt steɪz smɔl ju hæv kɛpt ðə ˈhæbət əˈlaɪv/

segments.text: Keeping the habit alive is very important.
segments.ipa: /ˈkipɪŋ ðə ˈhæbət əˈlaɪv ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: If you are busy, tired, or stressed, do the small version.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ɑr ˈbɪzi ˈtaɪərd ɔr strɛst du ðə smɔl ˈvɝʒən/

segments.text: Do not skip completely.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt skɪp kəmˈplitli/

segments.text: Say, "Today, I will do the smallest version."
segments.ipa: /seɪ təˈdeɪ aɪ wɪl du ðə ˈsmɔləst ˈvɝʒən/

segments.text: This protects your identity.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs prəˈtɛkts jɔr aɪˈdɛntɪˌti/

segments.text: You remain a person who shows up.
segments.ipa: /ju rɪˈmeɪn ə ˈpɝsən hu ʃoʊz ʌp/

segments.text: You remain a person who practices.
segments.ipa: /ju rɪˈmeɪn ə ˈpɝsən hu ˈpræktəsəz/

segments.text: For example, maybe your normal habit is 15 minutes of listening, but today you are very tired.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈmeɪbi jɔr ˈnɔrməl ˈhæbət ɪz ˈmɪnəts ʌv ˈlɪsənɪŋ bʌt təˈdeɪ ju ɑr ˈvɛri ˈtaɪərd/

segments.text: So, do 2 minutes.
segments.ipa: /soʊ du ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: That is okay.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: You kept the chain.
segments.ipa: /ju kɛpt ðə tʃeɪn/

segments.text: You told your brain, "I still practice English."
segments.ipa: /ju toʊld jɔr breɪn aɪ stɪl ˈpræktəs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: This is better than nothing.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈbɛtər ðæn ˈnʌθɪŋ/

segments.text: Many learners think if they cannot do a perfect session, they should do nothing.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz θɪŋk ɪf ðeɪ ˈkænɑt du ə pərˈfɛkt ˈsɛʃən ðeɪ ʃʊd du ˈnʌθɪŋ/

segments.text: This is a mistake.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə mɪˈsteɪk/

segments.text: Something small is much better than zero.
segments.ipa: /ˈsʌmθɪŋ smɔl ɪz mʌtʃ ˈbɛtər ðæn ˈzɪroʊ/

segments.text: Zero breaks the rhythm.
segments.ipa: /ˈzɪroʊ breɪks ðə ˈrɪðəm/

segments.text: A small action keeps the rhythm alive.
segments.ipa: /ə smɔl ˈækʃən kips ðə ˈrɪðəm əˈlaɪv/

segments.text: So, make it easy.
segments.ipa: /soʊ meɪk ɪt ˈizi/

segments.text: Another way to make English easy is to prepare everything before the habit.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər weɪ tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈizi ɪz tu priˈpɛr ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ bɪˈfɔr ðə ˈhæbət/

segments.text: If you waste time looking for materials, you may stop.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju weɪst taɪm ˈlʊkɪŋ fɔr məˈtɪriəlz ju meɪ stɑp/

segments.text: So, prepare your English practice in advance.
segments.ipa: /soʊ priˈpɛr jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈpræktəs ɪn ədˈvæns/

segments.text: Choose the podcast before morning.
segments.ipa: /tʃuz ðə ˈpɔdˌkæst bɪˈfɔr ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

segments.text: Open the page before study time.
segments.ipa: /ˈoʊpən ðə peɪdʒ bɪˈfɔr ˈstʌdi taɪm/

segments.text: Put the notebook on the desk.
segments.ipa: /pʊt ðə ˈnoʊtˌbʊk ɑn ðə dɛsk/

segments.text: Save the audio.
segments.ipa: /seɪv ðə ˈɑdiˌoʊ/

segments.text: Write the question you will answer.
segments.ipa: /raɪt ðə ˈkwɛstʃən ju wɪl ˈænsər/

segments.text: Prepare the vocabulary list.
segments.ipa: /priˈpɛr ðə voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri lɪst/

segments.text: When the time comes, you do not think too much.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ðə taɪm kʌmz ju du nɑt θɪŋk tu mʌtʃ/

segments.text: You just start.
segments.ipa: /ju dʒʌst stɑrt/

segments.text: Preparation removes friction.
segments.ipa: /ˌprɛpərˈeɪʃən riˈmuvz ˈfrɪkʃən/

segments.text: Friction means anything that makes the habit harder.
segments.ipa: /ˈfrɪkʃən minz ˈɛniˌθɪŋ ðæt meɪks ðə ˈhæbət ˈhɑrdər/

segments.text: If there is too much friction, the habit becomes less likely.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ðɛr ɪz tu mʌtʃ ˈfrɪkʃən ðə ˈhæbət bɪˈkʌmz lɛs ˈlaɪkli/

segments.text: If there is less friction, the habit becomes easier.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ðɛr ɪz lɛs ˈfrɪkʃən ðə ˈhæbət bɪˈkʌmz ˈiziər/

segments.text: For example, if you need to find a video, choose a topic, search for headphones,
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ɪf ju nid tu faɪnd ə ˈvɪdioʊ tʃuz ə ˈtɑpɪk sɝtʃ fɔr ˈhɛdˌfoʊnz/

segments.text: open your notebook, and decide what to do, you may feel tired.
segments.ipa: /ˈoʊpən jɔr ˈnoʊtˌbʊk ənd ˌdɪˈsaɪd wʌt tu du ju meɪ fil ˈtaɪərd/

segments.text: But if everything is ready, you press play.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ ɪz ˈrɛdi ju prɛs pleɪ/

segments.text: This is why simple systems matter.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ ˈsɪmpəl ˈsɪstəmz ˈmætər/

segments.text: Here is an easy English system.
segments.ipa: /hir ɪz æn ˈizi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈsɪstəm/

segments.text: Every morning, I listen to one saved podcast for 10 minutes.
segments.ipa: /ˈɛvəri ˈmɔrnɪŋ aɪ ˈlɪsən tu wʌn seɪvd ˈpɔdˌkæst fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: After listening, I choose one sentence and repeat it five times.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər ˈlɪsənɪŋ aɪ tʃuz wʌn ˈsɛntəns ənd rɪˈpit ɪt faɪv taɪmz/

segments.text: Then, I write that sentence in my notebook.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪ raɪt ðæt ˈsɛntəns ɪn maɪ ˈnoʊtˌbʊk/

segments.text: That is easy.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ˈizi/

segments.text: It is also clear and repeatable.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˈɔlsoʊ klɪr ənd rɪˈpitəbəl/

segments.text: You do not need to decide every day.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu ˌdɪˈsaɪd ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: You just do it.
segments.ipa: /ju dʒʌst du ɪt/

segments.text: Another part of making English easy is using the right level.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər pɑrt ʌv ˈmeɪkɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈizi ɪz ˈjuzɪŋ ðə raɪt ˈlɛvəl/

segments.text: Many learners choose materials that are too difficult because they think difficult means better.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz tʃuz məˈtɪriəlz ðæt ɑr tu ˈdɪfəkəlt bɪˈkɔz ðeɪ θɪŋk ˈdɪfəkəlt minz ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: But if the material is too difficult, your brain becomes tired.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ðə məˈtɪriəl ɪz tu ˈdɪfəkəlt jɔr breɪn bɪˈkʌmz ˈtaɪərd/

segments.text: You may feel stupid.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ fil ˈstupəd/

segments.text: You may stop.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ stɑp/

segments.text: Good practice should be understandable.
segments.ipa: /ɡʊd ˈpræktəs ʃʊd bi ˌʌndərˈstændəbəl/

segments.text: Not too easy, not too difficult.
segments.ipa: /nɑt tu ˈizi nɑt tu ˈdɪfəkəlt/

segments.text: If you understand most of it, you can learn new things without feeling lost.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ˌʌndərˈstænd moʊst ʌv ɪt ju kæn lɝn nu θɪŋz wɪˈθaʊt ˈfilɪŋ lɔst/

segments.text: This is easier and more effective than forcing yourself to understand something far above your level.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈiziər ənd mɔr ɪˈfɛktɪv ðæn ˈfɔrsɪŋ jərˈsɛlf tu ˌʌndərˈstænd ˈsʌmθɪŋ fɑr əˈbʌv jɔr ˈlɛvəl/

segments.text: Make it easy does not mean make it useless.
segments.ipa: /meɪk ɪt ˈizi dʌz nɑt min meɪk ɪt ˈjusləs/

segments.text: It means make it possible to repeat.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz meɪk ɪt ˈpɑsəbəl tu rɪˈpit/

segments.text: A habit that is repeated grows.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈhæbət ðæt ɪz rɪˈpitɪd ɡroʊz/

segments.text: A habit that is too difficult dies.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈhæbət ðæt ɪz tu ˈdɪfəkəlt daɪz/

segments.text: Another way to make English easy is to practice in small units.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər weɪ tu meɪk ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈizi ɪz tu ˈpræktəs ɪn smɔl ˈjunəts/

segments.text: Do not try to master a whole episode in one day.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt traɪ tu ˈmæstər ə hoʊl ˈɛpəˌsoʊd ɪn wʌn deɪ/

segments.text: Choose one paragraph, one sentence, one phrase, one question.
segments.ipa: /tʃuz wʌn ˈpærəˌɡræf wʌn ˈsɛntəns wʌn freɪz wʌn ˈkwɛstʃən/

segments.text: If pronunciation is difficult, practice one sound.
segments.ipa: /ɪf proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən ɪz ˈdɪfəkəlt ˈpræktəs wʌn saʊnd/

segments.text: If speaking is difficult, answer one question.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈspikɪŋ ɪz ˈdɪfəkəlt ˈænsər wʌn ˈkwɛstʃən/

segments.text: If vocabulary is difficult, learn three phrases.
segments.ipa: /ɪf voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri ɪz ˈdɪfəkəlt lɝn θri ˈfreɪzəz/

segments.text: If listening is difficult, repeat 30 seconds of audio.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈlɪsənɪŋ ɪz ˈdɪfəkəlt rɪˈpit ˈsɛkəndz ʌv ˈɑdiˌoʊ/

segments.text: Small units make practice manageable.
segments.ipa: /smɔl ˈjunəts meɪk ˈpræktəs ˈmænɪdʒəbəl/

segments.text: Manageable means you can handle it. Okay.
segments.ipa: /ˈmænɪdʒəbəl minz ju kæn ˈhændəl ɪt ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: Thank you so much for listening to English Unleashed.
segments.ipa: /θæŋk ju soʊ mʌtʃ fɔr ˈlɪsənɪŋ tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ənˈliʃt/

segments.text: I hope this episode helped you understand how atomic habits can help language learning.
segments.ipa: /aɪ hoʊp ðɪs ˈɛpəˌsoʊd hɛlpt ju ˌʌndərˈstænd haʊ əˈtɑmɪk ˈhæbəts kæn hɛlp ˈlæŋɡwədʒ ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: Listen again if you can.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən əˈɡɛn ɪf ju kæn/

segments.text: The first time, understand the main message.
segments.ipa: /ðə fɝst taɪm ˌʌndərˈstænd ðə meɪn ˈmɛsədʒ/

segments.text: The second time, notice the useful vocabulary.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈsɛkənd taɪm ˈnoʊtəs ðə ˈjusfəl voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri/

segments.text: The third time, shadow the sentences and practice speaking.
segments.ipa: /ðə θɝd taɪm ˈʃæˌdoʊ ðə ˈsɛntənsəz ənd ˈpræktəs ˈspikɪŋ/

segments.text: Bye for now.
segments.ipa: /baɪ fɔr naʊ/

segments.text: Mhm.
segments.ipa: /əmhəm/
